en.request: Research what's working on YouTube about personal finance for freelancers and tell me which video I should make.

reply.label: explosive · 14.1×
reply.text: An emergency fund for people with no fixed salary: 96K views on a channel that usually gets 6.8K.

reply.label: outlier · 6.2×
reply.text: How much to set aside for taxes as a freelancer: 41K views, against a channel normal of 6.6K.

reply.label: Pattern
reply.text: In 4 outliers, the title starts from having no fixed income and promises the math done: how much to save, how much to set aside.

reply.label: Saturated
reply.text: Expense spreadsheets and general budgeting tips: 31 videos, nearly all between 0.5× and 1.5× their channel's normal.

reply.label: Gap
reply.text: Retirement for freelancers: only 6 videos in the sample, and 3 of them beat 3×. There is demand, and few channels cover it.

reply.label: Caveats
reply.text: 112 videos from 88 channels, 58 with a measured normal. I left out 7 off-topic videos about landing clients.

reply.label: What to make
reply.text: Retirement for freelancers, with how much to put away each month right in the title. Take the outliers' angle, never their titles.
